evals.name: scope-cost-gate-unscoped-repo
evals.prompt:
/codebase-health:audit

Audit the whole codebase for drift between docs, config, code, and architecture.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes that an unscoped whole-repo run would fan out one subagent per doc/config/source file (a very large token cost), so it does NOT immediately dispatch discovery. It requires a scope or dimension filter, or confirms scope with the user, before fanning out.
expectations: Does NOT immediately fan out discovery subagents across the whole repository
Requires a scope or dimension filter, or asks the user to confirm scope, before dispatching discovery
States the cost rationale — a full unscoped fan-out spans every doc/config/source file at very large token cost

evals.name: review-only-gate-stops
evals.expected_output: Runs claim-extraction scoped to the single named file, presents the full Phase 3 findings report, then STOPS at the read-only gate without applying any fixes and without handing off to a remediation lane (no --fix given).
expectations: Presents the findings report and STOPS without applying any fixes
Does not modify, edit, or write any files
Does not hand off to /implementation:implement or /verification:confirm when --fix was not given
Scopes the audit to the named file only, not the whole repository
Includes the required 'Verified non-issues' section even in read-only mode

evals.name: fix-flag-delegates-not-inlines
evals.expected_output: Runs the scoped audit, presents the Phase 3 findings, then outputs an explicit user-directed suggestion to run /implementation:implement with those findings and then /verification:confirm (soft dependencies, used when installed) — without auto-invoking either skill and without running its own inline fix/verify/self-review/retrospect loop. When those plugins are not installed, it says so and treats the findings table as the manual handoff in the reported fix-priority order.
expectations: Presents the Phase 3 findings before any remediation
Suggests /implementation:implement for the fix and /verification:confirm for verification as user-directed next steps, described identically as suggestions rather than model-driven actions
Does not auto-invoke /implementation:implement or /verification:confirm — the user drives both
Does not re-implement a fix/verify/self-review/retrospect loop inside the audit skill
When the implementation/verification plugins are absent, states that and points to the findings table as the manual handoff instead of inlining the fix logic

evals.name: resolve-config-or-infer-and-persist
evals.expected_output: Resolves the tracked audit config (.claude/codebase-health.md and its other layers) for the documentation dimension. When it is present, uses its primary/verification sources; when absent, infers targets from the repo layout and offers to persist the inference via /codebase-health:setup rather than hardcoding a layout.
expectations: Attempts to resolve the tracked audit config before enumerating targets, rather than assuming a fixed repo layout
When config is absent, infers documentation targets from the repo and offers to persist them via the setup skill
Does not hardcode a specific repository's directory layout

evals.name: scoped-run-output-contract
evals.expected_output: Runs the scoped audit and presents findings in the exact required table with error/warning/info severity, followed by the required sections — verified non-issues, drift patterns, fix priority, enforcement escalation, and config-gap observations — with each finding confidence-tagged.
expectations: Presents findings in the required table with Severity, Category, File:Line, Description, and Verification columns using error/warning/info severity
Includes a 'Verified non-issues' section listing claims that were checked and found correct
Includes an enforcement-escalation assessment naming which automated check could catch each finding
Tags findings by confidence (verified / likely / needs-review) and separates needs-review items from confirmed findings
Includes a 'Config-gap observations' section naming dimensions, globs, or example-claims worth adding to the tracked config

evals.name: clean-scope-no-invented-findings
evals.prompt:
/codebase-health:audit package.json --config-only

Be thorough — I want to be sure nothing is drifting.
evals.expected_output: Verifies each factual claim in the named config file against reality. When everything checks out, it reports a clean bill of health with the verified non-issues list as proof of thoroughness, and does not fabricate marginal findings to justify the run.
expectations: Does not fabricate findings — reports only discrepancies actually verified against source
Presents a verified non-issues list showing what was checked
When no discrepancies are found, states explicitly that all claims verified as correct rather than padding with marginal issues
Includes a 'Config-gap observations' section naming dimensions, globs, or example-claims worth adding to the tracked config, even on a clean run

evals.name: boundary-route-to-harness-config
evals.prompt:
/codebase-health:audit

Check my .claude/settings.json and .mcp.json for schema drift, and tell me whether my hooks and permissions are misconfigured.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that settings.json / .mcp.json schema-drift and hook/permission validation is the adjacent harness-config lane, not this skill's factual-claim-drift lane. Declines to run its own claim-extraction fan-out over the settings schema. When the harness-config plugin is installed, routes the user to /harness-config:audit; otherwise states the request is out of scope.
expectations: Identifies settings.json / .mcp.json / hooks / permissions schema-drift as out of scope for this skill's claim-verification lane
When harness-config is installed, routes the user to /harness-config:audit rather than a bare or differently-named skill
When harness-config is not installed, states the request is out of scope instead of routing to a nonexistent skill
Does not run its own claim-extraction fan-out over the settings/MCP schema

evals.name: rendered-view-offered-not-built
evals.prompt:
/codebase-health:audit README.md --docs-only

(Fixture: interactive session; the visualization plugin is installed; no rendered-views scope sets medium; no --medium argument. The resolver prints a JSON line with medium null and the report line 'view: auto (plugin default)'. The audit finds two doc-drift findings.)
evals.expected_output: Presents the full Phase 3 report as usual, prints the resolver's report line 'view: auto (plugin default)', then makes one offer to render the findings through visualization:visualize, leaving the medium to that skill. It builds no HTML page itself.
expectations: Presents the full Phase 3 report before any rendered-view offer
Runs the shared medium resolver with --lane codebase-health:audit rather than reading rendered-views files itself
Prints the resolver's report line 'view: auto (plugin default)' as it stands
Offers to render the findings through visualization:visualize instead of building a view itself
Builds no HTML page or chart itself

evals.name: terminal-medium-drops-view-offer
evals.prompt:
/codebase-health:audit README.md --docs-only

(Fixture: interactive session; the visualization plugin is installed; the repository's tracked docs/conventions/rendered-views.yaml contains only 'medium: terminal'; no --medium argument. The resolver prints a JSON line with medium terminal and the report line 'view: terminal (team)'. The audit finds one doc-drift finding.)
evals.expected_output: Presents the full Phase 3 report, prints the resolver's report line 'view: terminal (team)', and makes no offer to render it through visualization:visualize, since the resolved medium is terminal.
expectations: Runs the shared medium resolver rather than reading docs/conventions/rendered-views.yaml itself
Prints the resolver's report line 'view: terminal (team)' as it stands
Makes no offer to render the report through visualization:visualize

evals.name: team-file-publishing-value-ignored
evals.prompt:
/codebase-health:audit README.md --docs-only

(Fixture: interactive session; the visualization plugin is installed; the repository's tracked docs/conventions/rendered-views.yaml contains only 'medium: artifact'; no --medium argument. The resolver prints a JSON line with medium null, the report line 'view: auto (plugin default)' and the notice 'notice: team docs/conventions/rendered-views.yaml sets medium: artifact; a team file never publishes, so it is ignored'. The audit finds one doc-drift finding, and the person accepts the rendered-view offer.)
evals.expected_output: Presents the full Phase 3 report, prints the resolver's report line and its team-file notice as they stand, then offers the rendered view. When the offer is taken, it invokes visualization:visualize without passing `artifact`, leaving the medium to that skill. Nothing is published on the team file's say-so.
expectations: Prints the resolver's report line and the notice that a team file never publishes
Offers the rendered view after the full report
Does not pass `artifact` to visualization:visualize when the offer is taken

evals.name: retired-file-local-value-keeps-view-local
evals.prompt:
/codebase-health:audit README.md --docs-only

(Fixture: interactive session; the visualization plugin is installed; first run in this project; ~/.claude/rendered-views.md contains only 'medium: terminal'; no other rendered-views scope sets medium and the plugin's medium option is auto; no --medium argument. The resolver prints a JSON line with medium terminal, the report line 'view: terminal (retired ~/.claude/rendered-views.md)' and the notice 'notice: ~/.claude/rendered-views.md is retired but still keeps the view local (it sets medium: terminal); set it in docs/conventions/rendered-views.local.yaml instead; per user, the codebase-health plugin's medium option also works'. The audit finds one doc-drift finding.)
evals.expected_output: Presents the full Phase 3 report, prints the resolver's report line and its retired-file notice as they stand, and makes no offer to render it through visualization:visualize, since the resolved medium is terminal. It does not open or read ~/.claude/rendered-views.md itself.
expectations: Does not read ~/.claude/rendered-views.md itself
Prints the resolver's report line and its notice that ~/.claude/rendered-views.md is retired but still keeps the view local
Makes no offer to render the report through visualization:visualize

evals.name: retired-file-publishing-value-ignored
evals.prompt:
/codebase-health:audit README.md --docs-only

(Fixture: interactive session; the visualization plugin is installed; first run in this project; ~/.claude/rendered-views.md contains only 'medium: artifact'; no other rendered-views scope sets medium and the plugin's medium option is auto; no --medium argument. The resolver prints a JSON line with medium null, the report line 'view: auto (plugin default)' and the notice 'notice: ~/.claude/rendered-views.md is no longer read (it sets medium: artifact); set it in docs/conventions/rendered-views.local.yaml instead; it publishes only while that file is untracked and gitignored; per user, the codebase-health plugin's medium option also works'. The audit finds one doc-drift finding, and the person accepts the rendered-view offer.)
evals.expected_output: Presents the full Phase 3 report, prints the resolver's report line and its retired-file notice as they stand, then offers the rendered view. When the offer is taken, it invokes visualization:visualize without passing `artifact`, leaving the medium to that skill. It does not open or read ~/.claude/rendered-views.md itself.
expectations: Does not read ~/.claude/rendered-views.md itself
Prints the resolver's notice that ~/.claude/rendered-views.md is no longer read
Offers the rendered view after the full report
Does not pass `artifact` to visualization:visualize when the offer is taken
